sentences.en: Welcome to ADSP, the podcast, episode 195, recorded on July 22nd, 2024.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSP 播客第 195 集，录制于 2024 年 7 月 22 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor, and today with my co-host Bryce, we record live from CPP North 2024.
sentences.zh: 我是 Connor，今天我和我的联合主持人 Bryce 在 2024 年 C++ 北美大会现场进行录制。

sentences.en: We start off by interviewing David Olson, and then things devolve into pure chaos.
sentences.zh: 我们先采访了 David Olson，然后场面就陷入了纯粹的混乱。

sentences.en: Other individuals you'll hear from are Tristan Brindle, Christian Shaker, Ben Dean, and a special guest with a special announcement.
sentences.zh: 你还会听到 Tristan Brindle、Christian Shaker、Ben Dean 的声音，还有一位带着特别公告的特邀嘉宾。

sentences.en: What are we doing here?
sentences.zh: 我们在这儿干什么呢？

sentences.en: This is my mind.
sentences.zh: 这是我的想法。

sentences.zh: 伙计们，我们现在在多伦多微软大楼的 44 楼，2024 年 C++ 北美大会现场。

sentences.zh: 还有那座可爱的加拿大国家电视塔（CN Tower）。

sentences.zh: 你知道，在纽约，我们有大约 10 座标志性建筑。

sentences.zh: 我们有克莱斯勒大厦。

sentences.zh: 我们有帝国大厦。

sentences.zh: 我们有花旗集团中心、口红大厦、世界贸易中心一号大楼。

sentences.zh: 但在多伦多，他们只有一座，那就是加拿大国家电视塔。

sentences.en: But it's a very nice building.
sentences.zh: 但那确实是一座非常漂亮的建筑。

sentences.en: You know, we have 10, but they've got one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们有 10 座，而他们只有一座。

sentences.zh: 它比纽约那 10 座中的任何一座都要高。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Let's go, David.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧，David。

sentences.en: Thank you for defending Canada.
sentences.zh: 感谢你为加拿大辩护。

sentences.en: And we're here with our first guest of the night, who we're going to talk to quickly because he needs to go to bed.
sentences.zh: 我们现在和今晚的第一位嘉宾在一起，我们要快点聊，因为他得去睡觉了。

sentences.en: Mr. David Olson, our co-worker.
sentences.zh: David Olson 先生，我们的同事。

sentences.en: Hey.
sentences.zh: 嘿。

sentences.en: A long-time listener on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 播客的长期听众。

sentences.en: Is this your first time at C++ North?
sentences.zh: 这是你第一次参加 C++ 北美大会吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: What were you here to talk about today?
sentences.zh: 你今天来是想聊些什么？

sentences.en: Today, I talked about reflection.
sentences.zh: 今天我聊了反射。

sentences.en: That's coming in C++ 26.
sentences.zh: 那将出现在 C++ 26 标准中。

sentences.en: What are the most important three things people should know about reflection?
sentences.zh: 关于反射，人们最应该知道的三件事是什么？

sentences.en: The conclusions of my talk were, one, it's coming.
sentences.zh: 我演讲的结论是，第一，它要来了。

sentences.en: Two, remember that it is compile time only.
sentences.zh: 第二，记住它仅在编译时生效。

sentences.en: So you've got to up your compile time programming game.
sentences.zh: 所以你得提升你的编译时编程水平。

sentences.en: And three, the most useful thing is it helps you get rid of boilerplate code.
sentences.zh: 第三，它最有用的地方在于能帮你摆脱样板代码。

sentences.en: Things that you did manually, the tedious manual stuff that you've been doing, some of that can be replaced with reflection.
sentences.zh: 那些你以前手动完成的、繁琐的手动工作，其中一些可以用反射来替代。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: And I actually think this might be a first because I think this is the first time we've had a C++ compiler engineer who's actively working on a production C++ compiler on the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我真的认为这可能是第一次，因为我觉得这是我们第一次在播客上请到一位正在积极开发生产级 C++ 编译器的编译器工程师。

sentences.en: So, David, you work on which compiler?
sentences.zh: 那么，David，你在开发哪款编译器？

sentences.en: NVIDIA's HPC C++ compiler called NVC++.
sentences.zh: NVIDIA 的高性能计算 C++ 编译器，叫 NVC++。

sentences.en: And what is it like to work on a C++ compiler?
sentences.zh: 开发 C++ 编译器是什么感觉？

sentences.en: It's fun.
sentences.zh: 很有趣。

sentences.en: It's challenging.
sentences.zh: 很有挑战性。

sentences.en: Part of my job is to just sort of keep the whole thing together, keep it running.
sentences.zh: 我的部分工作就是维持整个系统的运转，保持它的稳定性。

sentences.en: So I've got to keep all the pieces, make sure it works correctly, compiles code correctly.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须照看好所有组件，确保它能正常工作，正确地编译代码。

sentences.en: What is the hardest part about working through problems in a C++ compiler versus working through problems in, like, a regular application?
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 编译器中解决问题，与在常规应用程序中解决问题相比，最难的部分是什么？

sentences.en: Some things are easier.
sentences.zh: 有些事情反而更容易。

sentences.en: It's pretty much always reproducible.
sentences.zh: 它几乎总是可重现的。

sentences.en: Because it's a single thing, we don't have the concurrency, we don't have random inputs, you can reproduce your inputs.
sentences.zh: 因为它是一个单一的系统，我们没有并发问题，没有随机输入，你可以重现你的输入。

sentences.en: That part's easier.
sentences.zh: 那部分更容易。

sentences.en: So you heard it here first, people.
sentences.zh: 所以大家听到了吧。

sentences.en: C++ compiler is an easy job.
sentences.zh: 开发 C++ 编译器是一份轻松的工作。

sentences.en: No, I said less hard.
sentences.zh: 不，我说的是没那么难。

sentences.en: There's other domains have their own very hard problems that I don't have.
sentences.zh: 其他领域有他们自己非常棘手的问题，而我没有。

sentences.en: But these data structures get so big, it's hard to navigate through them and know what the compiler is doing.
sentences.zh: 但这些数据结构变得太大了，很难在其中导航并弄清楚编译器在做什么。

sentences.en: And some of the hardest problems aren't so much debugging in the compiler, but figuring out why applications are not behaving correctly.
sentences.zh: 而且一些最难的问题与其说是编译器里的调试，不如说是弄清楚为什么应用程序表现不正常。

sentences.en: Is it a bug in the code?
sentences.zh: 是代码里的 Bug 吗？

sentences.en: Are we generating?
sentences.zh: 是我们生成的……

sentences.en: Is the compiler generating bad code?
sentences.zh: 是编译器生成了糟糕的代码吗？

sentences.en: Or things like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: That can be very hard.
sentences.zh: 那可能非常困难。

sentences.en: When application just gets the wrong answer, it can be very hard to figure out why.
sentences.zh: 当应用程序得到错误的结果时，找出原因可能非常困难。

sentences.en: On the sidefall, Connor, did you need to interject something AV-related?
sentences.zh: 顺便问一下，Connor，你需要插播一些关于音频设备的事情吗？

sentences.en: I was going to say, we should probably move over here, because I don't have headphones on.
sentences.zh: 我本来想说，我们应该搬到这边来，因为我没戴耳机。

sentences.en: So, listener, if the audio quality is too loud, because...
sentences.zh: 所以，听众朋友们，如果音频质量太吵，因为……

sentences.en: It's Connor's fault.
sentences.zh: 那是 Connor 的错。

sentences.en: We made this mistake at C++ on C, 2023.
sentences.zh: 我们在 2023 年的 C++ on Sea 大会上就犯过这个错误。

sentences.en: We stood a little bit too close to folks.
sentences.zh: 我们站得离人群太近了。

sentences.en: And it wasn't until Sean, you and I, moved to the outdoor thing that the audio quality...
sentences.zh: 直到 Sean 你和我搬到户外，音频质量才……

sentences.en: It was still audible?
sentences.zh: 还能听得见吗？

sentences.en: I thought you said that that was part of the...
sentences.zh: 我以为你说那是……的一部分。

sentences.en: It would be part of the ambiance to have that background noise.
sentences.zh: 有那种背景噪音会成为氛围的一部分。

sentences.en: We still got the ambiance now, but now it's quieter.
sentences.zh: 我们现在依然有氛围感，但现在安静多了。

sentences.en: A little bit of background noise makes for good ambiance.
sentences.zh: 一点背景噪音能营造出很好的氛围。

sentences.en: Fair enough.
sentences.zh: 有道理。

sentences.en: So, David, how long have you worked on C++ compilers?
sentences.zh: 那么，David，你从事 C++ 编译器开发多久了？

sentences.en: I've been in this job for eight years.
sentences.zh: 我做这份工作已经八年了。

sentences.en: 30 years ago, my first job was on the front end of a C++ compiler.
sentences.zh: 30 年前，我的第一份工作是在 C++ 编译器的前端。

sentences.en: 30 years ago?
sentences.zh: 30 年前？

sentences.en: Do you know how old we were 30 years ago?
sentences.zh: 你知道 30 年前我们多大吗？

sentences.en: You weren't born yet.
sentences.zh: 你还没出生呢。

sentences.en: I was.
sentences.zh: 我出生了。

sentences.en: I was three.
sentences.zh: 我当时三岁。

sentences.en: I was three.
sentences.zh: 我当时三岁。

sentences.en: Good sirs.
sentences.zh: 好先生们。

sentences.en: I was three.
sentences.zh: 我当时三岁。

sentences.en: My birthday was yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我的生日是昨天。

sentences.en: You knew I'd find a way to work that end of the episode.
sentences.zh: 你就知道我会想办法在节目结尾提这一茬。

sentences.en: But I got a cake today.
sentences.zh: 但我今天确实收到了蛋糕。

sentences.en: And I did get a cake today.
sentences.zh: 我今天确实收到了蛋糕。

sentences.en: My dear friend Kristen and my girlfriend surprised me with a cake.
sentences.zh: 我亲爱的朋友 Kristen 和我的女朋友给了我一个惊喜蛋糕。

sentences.en: And everyone in the room sang happy birthday to them.
sentences.zh: 屋里的每个人都为他们唱了生日歌。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: That is true.
sentences.zh: 那是真的。

sentences.en: But so, 30 years ago, what was that first compiler that you worked on?
sentences.zh: 那么，30 年前，你参与开发的第一个编译器是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it was the Rational C++ compiler, which nobody has heard of because it was not a good success.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是 Rational C++ 编译器，没人听说过，因为它并不成功。

sentences.en: Why was it not a good success?
sentences.zh: 为什么它不成功？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: We didn't have, there wasn't enough special about it.
sentences.zh: 我们没有……它没什么特别之处。

sentences.en: Okay, all right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: Now, Connor said a whoa when he heard Rational C++.
sentences.zh: 刚才 Connor 听到 Rational C++ 时发出了一声惊叹。

sentences.en: And I think Connor at least has heard about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得 Connor 至少听说过它。

sentences.en: I have heard of Rational.
sentences.zh: 我听说过 Rational。

sentences.en: You haven't heard of Rational?
sentences.zh: 你没听说过 Rational？

sentences.en: I have not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: I have not.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: The reason I went whoa is that that's a compiler.
sentences.zh: 我之所以惊叹，是因为那是一个编译器。

sentences.en: I was expecting, what do they call it?
sentences.zh: 我本来以为是，他们叫它什么来着？

sentences.en: Not Turbo Pasca, but wasn't there a Turbo C++?
sentences.zh: 不是 Turbo Pascal，但当时不是有个 Turbo C++ 吗？

sentences.en: There was.
sentences.zh: 确实有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And then there was also.
sentences.zh: 然后还有。

sentences.en: And that was by Borland, right?
sentences.zh: 那是 Borland 公司的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that became the Borland compiler.
sentences.zh: 后来变成了 Borland 编译器。

sentences.en: So, then what did you work on after this compiler?
sentences.zh: 那么，在这个编译器之后你又做了什么？

sentences.en: I moved on to other programming tools.
sentences.zh: 我转向了其他编程工具。

sentences.en: I spent a long time.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间。

sentences.en: I spent 20 years working on programming tools of some sort.
sentences.zh: 我花了 20 年时间从事各种编程工具的开发。

sentences.en: So, after the compiler, I think I worked on Rational Rows.
sentences.zh: 所以，在编译器之后，我想我参与了 Rational Rose 的开发。

sentences.en: What was Rational Rows?
sentences.zh: Rational Rose 是什么？

sentences.en: It was a UML modeling tool.
sentences.zh: 它是一个 UML 建模工具。

sentences.en: That sounds like fun.
sentences.zh: 听起来很有趣。

sentences.en: And then worked on a different UML modeling tool and several things in the UML modeling space.
sentences.zh: 然后我又参与了另一个 UML 建模工具，以及 UML 建模领域的几项工作。

sentences.en: Then moved into, I was a build engineer.
sentences.zh: 后来我转行做了构建工程师。

sentences.en: Sort of got a whole bunch of teams to work together.
sentences.zh: 算是让一大堆团队协同工作。

sentences.en: We had a common build for a large part of Rational organization.
sentences.zh: 我们为 Rational 组织的大部分部门提供了一个通用的构建系统。

sentences.en: And I wrote tooling for that and ran that.
sentences.zh: 我为此编写了工具并负责运行它。

sentences.en: And then you.
sentences.zh: 然后你……

sentences.en: Which I learned a lot in that experience.
sentences.zh: 那段经历让我学到了很多。

sentences.en: What is UML for listeners who have not been exposed to it?
sentences.zh: 对于还没接触过 UML 的听众，UML 是什么？

sentences.en: Unified modeling language is what it stands for.
sentences.zh: 它代表统一建模语言。

sentences.en: And it is for people who want to draw pictures of their application design.
sentences.zh: 它是为那些想要绘制应用程序设计图的人准备的。

sentences.en: Is UML a good idea?
sentences.zh: UML 是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: It had its uses.
sentences.zh: 它曾经有它的用途。

sentences.en: Some people found it very useful.
sentences.zh: 有些人觉得它非常有用。

sentences.en: It can be useful, but it wasn't widely successful.
sentences.zh: 它可能有用，但并没有取得广泛的成功。

sentences.en: So, it has fallen out of favor.
sentences.zh: 所以，它已经不再受宠了。

sentences.en: It wasn't successful enough in the long run for people to keep making tools for it.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，它还不够成功，不足以让人们持续为它开发工具。

sentences.en: So, was the idea that you would like almost like visually program, like you would visually represent parts of your program?
sentences.zh: 那么，当时的想法是你想进行某种视觉化编程，就像视觉化地表示程序的各个部分吗？

sentences.en: Or was it just like solely a modeling thing?
sentences.zh: 还是说它仅仅是一个建模工具？

sentences.en: Like I never really understood that aspect of UML.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有真正理解 UML 的那个方面。

sentences.en: It was a model, well, some visual to it, but more a modeling thing.
sentences.zh: 它是一个模型，嗯，有一些视觉效果，但更多的是一种建模工具。

sentences.en: So, you had boxes or some shape to represent your classes.
sentences.zh: 所以，你用方框或某种形状来表示你的类。

sentences.en: And you drew the arrows between them for the relationships between your classes.
sentences.zh: 然后在它们之间画箭头来表示类之间的关系。

sentences.en: And there were all sorts of other shapes to represent other things in your application.
sentences.zh: 还有各种各样的其他形状来表示应用程序中的其他事物。

sentences.en: And draw how they were connected together.
sentences.zh: 并画出它们是如何连接在一起的。

sentences.en: And it was possible to generate some code directly from those models.
sentences.zh: 而且可以直接从这些模型中生成一些代码。

sentences.en: That was the big hype is that there was this idea that you could design visually the structure of your code and then use that to, to some extent, generate the shape of your code.
sentences.zh: 当时最大的炒作点在于，人们认为你可以视觉化地设计代码结构，然后利用这一点，在一定程度上生成代码的雏形。

sentences.en: And then that would be a starting point.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个起点。

sentences.en: Visual programming.
sentences.zh: 视觉化编程。

sentences.en: Not something we've talked about on this episode before, but I think a lot of people in the programming world got started in the robotics field as a kid.
sentences.zh: 虽然我们在本期节目中之前没有讨论过，但我认为编程界很多人小时候都是从机器人领域开始接触编程的。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of robotics frameworks and a lot of like early educational programming frameworks where you program visually.
sentences.zh: 有很多机器人框架和许多早期的教育编程框架，你可以在其中进行视觉化编程。

sentences.en: You drag different code blocks and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你可以拖拽不同的代码块之类的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，有很多。

sentences.en: I have been a coach for middle school Lego robotics teaMs.
sentences.zh: 我曾担任过初中乐高机器人队的教练。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And yes, the programming is very visual.
sentences.zh: 没错，这种编程方式非常直观。

sentences.en: Is there a language?
sentences.zh: 有专门的语言吗？

sentences.en: I know Scratch is a language, but is there a Lego language that...
sentences.zh: 我知道 Scratch 是一种语言，但有没有一种乐高语言……

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't remember what it's called, but it's, it's, it's, it's mostly, it's mostly the visual.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不记得它叫什么了，但它主要是视觉化的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
